findings.text: named_lane_request_waiting passes project=project to runs.list_live, so the waiting population is scoped to the dispatching project while its own docstring at placement.py:118-127 states the population is host-wide because one reservation seats every project's workers. A named-lane request queued in project B therefore does not hold the reserve for a local dispatch in project A, and project A fills the shared roster the request is waiting behind — the starvation the reserve exists to prevent, in the multi-project case. Dropping the project= argument is the whole repair.

The queued reason is hardcoded as "the placement reservation's roster is full (occupancy/limit)" at preparation.py:1149 and again at :1342-1345, but _refuse_over_concurrency_ceiling raises RosterFull from whichever of the roster, partition-&-memory bound actually binds (dispatch_admission.py:301-322), so a dispatch held at the cores bound is reported to the coordinator as a full roster with occupancy from this backend's live runs and limit from the binding bound. The accurate bound_refusal_text survives only in the unprinted 'detail' key, which makes the coordinator-facing reason wrong precisely for the cores-bound case the plan's done_when names.

The done_when requires a codex dispatch held at the cores bound or the roster cap to be queued, but every bound case in this module occupies the roster (LIMIT occupants) and asserts the roster path; nothing binds a partition-cores or memory bound, so a regression that refused at those bounds alone — the half of dispatch_admission.py:301-322 the diff widens with no case of its own — would leave all eight cases green.
